meta.name: Zancut camera rule book
meta.phoneFirst: Every top-level framing number is the 9:16 value. formats['16:9'] inside a size/angle lists only what changes for 16:9.

conventions.frame: x 0 = left edge, 1 = right edge (fraction of frame width). y 0 = top edge, 1 = bottom edge (fraction of frame height). Values below 0 or above 1 mean outside the frame (used for horizons).
conventions.landmarkOffset: 'chin+0.7head' = 0.7 head-heights BELOW the chin. Minus = above. 1 head = top of skull to chin of THAT character (from the body chart, Brief 6). Default landmark positions are in landmarks below.
conventions.headroom: gap between the top of the head (hair/cap included) and the frame top, as a fraction of frame height. Negative = the head is cropped.
conventions.eyeLine: height of the eyes in the frame, fraction from the top.
conventions.cameraHeight: metres above the ground under the camera. 'eye' = the subject's eye height. 'eye+0.3' = 0.3 m above it.
conventions.horizon: fraction from the top. For a level camera the horizon is the line at camera height: it cuts every standing person at the same real height as the camera.
conventions.facing: yaw in degrees around the vertical axis: 0 = toward camera (front), +-45 = three-quarter, +-90 = side, 180 = back. + means the nose points to screen right.
conventions.screenDir: +1 = person faces/moves toward screen right, -1 = toward screen left, 0 = toward or away from camera.
conventions.time: seconds; f = frames at 30 fps. Ranges are [min, max].
conventions.metresAtSubject: All metre framing (frame width/height) is measured at the depth of the subject's feet. Convert with the engine's own scale-by-depth.
conventions.sizeLadder: ladder index used by the jump-cut rule: extremeWide 0, wide 1, full 2, mediumWide 3, medium 4, mediumClose 5, closeUp 6, extremeClose 7. insert, twoShot and group map onto the ladder by their actual framing (field ladderEquivalent).

engineAssumptions: Camera = lookAt(x, y) + frame width + tilt (roll) + camera height; frame height follows the format.

Level camera with a shift: verticals stay vertical. A real camera that pitches up/down (3-point perspective) is NOT available; the rule book fakes pitch with horizon position, camera height and what shows behind the head.
People: front, three, side, back views; full body or waist up; head turn and eye targets free.
Most set pieces: front view only, drawn as seen from about 1.5 m camera height (h_ref).
Layers have depth; size and height on screen follow depth. If the engine can move the camera in depth (z), moves marked 'dolly' get real parallax; otherwise they fall back to zoom.
howToUse: 1. Pick a recipe for the story moment (recipes).
2. For each shot, resolve size -> frame top/bottom from landmarks, angle -> camera height and horizon, move -> keyframes.
3. Run every rule in rules[] on the planned shot list; apply 'fix' for failures.
4. Check pace against style.pace for the film length.

priorityKey.must: breaking it looks like a mistake to any viewer
priorityKey.should: breaking it looks amateur; allowed with a reason tag

landmarks.note: Default positions in head units down from headTop. Replace with the measured body chart (Brief 6) per character; every framing rule here uses landmark names, so it adapts automatically.

seatedAdult.note: chair seat 0.45 m; on a mat or pati the hips are at 0 m. Use these as 'eye' for seated subjects.

joints.note: Frame edges must not cross a person inside these bands (head units). Cut in the 'safeCuts' instead.

safeZones.note: Platform UI covers these bands. Faces, captions, text and the key prop stay inside the 'keySafe' box. Values are fractions of the frame. Measured on 1080x1920; apps change their UI, so re-check yearly.

burnedInCaptions.note: Above the Reels/Shorts tray. For TikTok-only posts y 0.66-0.72 is fine.

9:16.composition: Centre-weighted. One subject per frame by default; two only when stacked in depth or very close. Vertical motion (rise, fall, tilt) reads strongest.
9:16.lookRoomSingle: face centre x 0.42-0.47 when facing right (mirror for left); centred 0.5 when facing camera
9:16.twoPeopleSideBySide: only from mediumWide outward, or when they stand <= 0.6 m apart; otherwise stack in depth or use OTS

safeZones.note: Keep text inside the central 90 % and action inside 93 % (broadcast convention).

16:9.composition: Rule of thirds: face on the third line opposite the look direction; two-shots side by side work from medium outward.
16:9.lookRoomSingle: face centre x 0.33-0.40 when facing right (mirror for left)
16:9.phoneLetterbox: Watched on an upright phone a 16:9 film fills only ~32 % of the screen height: frame one size tighter than you would for TV.

formats.dualDelivery: Render each format natively from the same shot spec (same landmarks, same camera height). Never crop 16:9 to 9:16: a crop keeps only 32 % of the width.

frameFromLandmarks.frameHeight: H = (bottomLandmark - topLandmark) / (1 - headroom - footroom) * head_m   [footroom only for full shots]
frameFromLandmarks.lookAtY: frame centre height in metres = headTopHeight + headroom*H - H/2 (world height above the subject's ground)

horizon.rule: Level camera at height h: every point at height h, at any depth, lands on the horizon line. So the horizon cuts every standing person at the same body height (h).
horizon.formula: horizonY = (pointOnSubjectAtHeight_h - frameTop) / frameHeight, in head units: ((stature - h)/head_m - topHeads) / frameHeightHeads

behindTheHead.rule: What the background shows behind a subject's eyes tells the viewer the camera height even when the horizon is out of frame.
behindTheHead.formula: backgroundHeightBehindEyes = h + (eyeHeight - h) * (D / d)   (d = subject depth, D = background depth)
behindTheHead.example: man eyes 1.54 m, d 2 m, wall at 4 m: eye level -> 1.54 m (mid wall); h 0.9 -> 2.18 m (top of wall / ceiling line); h 2.4 -> 0.68 m (lower wall, floor shows above the shoulders)

floorBand.rule: The ground strip between two depths appears with a height proportional to camera height h.

surfaceTop.rule: A horizontal surface at height s shows its top only when s < h, its underside only when s > h, and is edge-on when |s-h| < 0.08 m.
surfaceTop.frontPieceTolerance: Front-view pieces are drawn for h_ref 1.5 m. Top-band ratio = (h - s)/(1.5 - s). Ratio 0.7-1.4 passes as drawn; outside that, crop the surface out of frame, cover it with foreground, or scale the piece's top layer by the ratio if the piece has its top as a separate layer.

geometry.depthScale: screen size = realSize * k / depth. Two people of equal height: size ratio = depthFar / depthNear.

lensFeel.wide: subject 0.8-1.5 m from camera: near things swell, background shrinks fast (low-angle power, worm's eye, comedy)
lensFeel.telephoto: subject 10-30 m with a tight frame: depth compresses, crowds and rickshaw traffic stack up (Dhaka streets, markets)
lensFeel.howInFlat2D: Lens = camera distance. Same frame size from a longer distance = background layers keep their size (compressed). From a short distance = background tiny, foreground huge.

dutchCoverage.rule: Rolling the frame by angle t needs the set to cover w' = w*cos t + h*sin t and h' = w*sin t + h*cos t.
dutchCoverage.note: multipliers of the frame width and height the set must cover; or shrink frameW by the width factor.

panSpeedLimit.rule: Without motion blur, nothing should move more than 0.0106 of the frame's SHORT side per frame (about 11 px at 1080). This is the cinema '7-second rule' (24 fps, edge to edge in 7 s) carried to 30 fps.
panSpeedLimit.withMotionBlur: halve the minimum times; blur length = per-frame travel * 0.5
panSpeedLimit.exception: When the camera follows a moving subject, judge the subject (nearly still in frame), not the background.

blur.depthOfField: blurRadius = k * |1/d - 1/dFocus|, clamp to 3 % of the short side. k chosen so the main background (2x subject depth) gets 0.6-1.0 % of the short side.

sizeClassify.note: Classify any planned or rendered shot by headFraction = (projected head height of the main subject) / frameHeight. Boundaries are geometric means between the canonical sizes below.

subjectPos.x: on a vertical third (0.33 or 0.67) in 16:9; x 0.4-0.6 in 9:16

extremeWide.drawDetail: people can be simplified silhouettes (no face features) below head height 0.012 of frame height
extremeWide.use: open a film or a new place (village, river, city); show a person small against the world (lost, alone, a long journey); time and weather changes (monsoon clouds, dusk); end a film
extremeWide.avoid: any shot where we must read a face or a small action; more than one in a row unless it is a journey montage; under 1.5 s (nothing reads)
extremeWide.flat2d: Cheapest shot to make beautiful: 4-5 depth layers (sky, far trees/hills, midground houses, ground band, foreground grass/branch). A slow parallaxDrift (2-4 % of frame width) keeps it alive.

9:16.note: Tall frame: lots of sky or lots of ground. Put the horizon on a third: low (0.6-0.7) for sky/clouds/rain drama, high (0.36-0.45) for fields, river, roads. Subject inside keySafe x 0.06-0.82.

16:9.note: Classic wide vista; subject on a vertical third, small.

wide.use: establish where everyone is before cutting closer (geography for the 180 line); entrances and exits; physical comedy; group blocking; a person in their room/shop/field
wide.avoid: dialogue that matters (faces too small: lip-sync not readable under head 0.06 of frame); staying wide for an emotional line
wide.lipSync: Head below 0.06 of frame height: simple open/close mouth is enough; below 0.03 no mouth animation needed.
wide.flat2d: Needs the full set front view plus floor/ground band. Horizon passes through standing people at camera height (see geometry.horizon).

9:16.note: Person 0.2-0.45 of frame height. Use the height: ceiling fan + floor, or sky + road. Two people side by side fit easily here.

16:9.note: Room for 3-6 people across.

full.use: body language that needs the whole body (a slump, a dance, a namaz rakat seen from the side or behind, a child jumping); a walk; costume reveal; a person entering
full.avoid: feet cut at the ankles (use belowFeet or cut at midShin = mediumWide); dialogue longer than one line
full.flat2d: Contact shadow under feet is mandatory (an ellipse 1.1 x shoe length wide, 0.25 of that tall, 20-35 % darker than the floor). Floating feet are the first thing that looks cheap.

9:16.note: Frame width ~4.9 heads (man 1.08 m): one person fills the frame nicely; feet sit under the caption tray, which is fine (feet are not key content).

16:9.note: Frame width ~15.5 heads (3.4 m): lots of side room; place the person on a third, look room ahead.

mediumWide.use: two people standing and talking in 9:16 (both fit when <= 0.6 m apart); gestures with both arms; a person holding a big thing (sack of rice, school bag, cricket bat); shop counters
mediumWide.avoid: cutting exactly at the knee (the joint band 5.2-5.6 head); using it for an emotional peak (go tighter)
mediumWide.flat2d: Legs are in frame down to the thighs: walk cycles and sitting poses must be the full-body rig.

9:16.note: Frame width ~3.2 heads (0.69 m for a man): both arms with gestures fit. The best 9:16 shot for acting with the hands.

16:9.note: Frame width ~10 heads: a natural two-shot size for people 0.8-1.2 m apart.

medium.use: the default dialogue size; explaining with one hand; eating, writing, phone use; a narrator/presenter talking to camera
medium.avoid: a whole scene at this size (the 'one long medium' problem the brief names); cutting at the belt line (waistLine band) or at the wrists when hands hang
medium.flat2d: Waist-up rig is enough. Hands that rise above the frame bottom must be drawn; hands below it can be skipped.

9:16.note: Frame width ~2.1 heads: the shoulders fill the width, upper arms cut by the sides. Gestures leave the frame: for big gestures use mediumWide.

16:9.note: Frame width ~6.5 heads: real look room on the facing side; a medium two-shot works when the two are <= 0.75 m apart.

mediumClose.use: the workhorse of phone dialogue: lines that matter, listening reactions, a thought; most 9:16 singles live here
mediumClose.avoid: cutting MCU to CU of the same person with no other change (step 1.45 is the minimum; add a view change or a push); a person who is not feeling or saying anything
mediumClose.flat2d: Face expression must be readable: eyes, brows and mouth shapes matter more than the body here.

9:16.note: Frame width ~1.5 heads: face plus a bit of shoulder; look room is tiny, so show direction with head turn (three view) and eye direction.

16:9.note: Classic TV dialogue single.

subjectPos.x: 9:16 face centre 0.46-0.54 (direction shown by yaw and eyes)

closeUp.use: emotion that matters; a reaction; a decision; the moment a feeling changes; the end of a scene
closeUp.avoid: more than 3 in a row; a close-up of someone who is not feeling anything; during sajdah; on a young child's crying face held longer than 2 s (feels exploitative); hiding bad animation (close-ups magnify it)
closeUp.flat2d: The face fills the frame: eyes, blinks, brows and mouth must be animated; a held face with no blink for > 3 s looks dead (blink every 2-4 s).

9:16.note: Frame width ~1.0 head (man 0.22 m): the face fills the width. This is THE phone shot.

16:9.note: Frame width ~3 heads: look room on the facing side.

faceFill.note: forehead to under the chin, cheeks cropped; 9:16 default

eyes.note: 16:9 default (both eyes); in 9:16 only ONE eye fits: frame width 0.35 head

mouth.note: a word that matters, a smile starting, biting a lip

oneEye.note: 9:16 eye ECU: the eye at y 0.4-0.5

extremeClose.use: a shock or realisation peak (eyes widen); tension before an action (eyes narrow); the hidden truth in a smile; a tear
extremeClose.avoid: dialogue; more than 1 per 20 s; any character whose face design has no detail at this scale (flat-colour faces can look empty: test it)
extremeClose.flat2d: Magnification is 3-5x a medium shot: needs a face drawn with enough shape detail (iris, eyelid line, lip shape). If the face design is very simple, use closeUp + zoomPunch instead.

9:16.note: Use faceFill or oneEye or mouth.

16:9.note: the 'eyes' strip

insert.ladderEquivalent: closeUp (for jump-cut tests treat the object as the subject)
insert.magnificationCheck: magnification = mediumShotFrameWidth(of the character using it) / insertFrameWidth. <= 3: front-view prop is fine. 3-6: needs clean big shapes (no thin details lost). > 6: needs a detail drawing of the prop.
insert.holdItUp: Flat things (letter, phone screen, photo, money, exam result, ID card) work in FRONT view if the character holds them up facing the camera. A thing lying on a table needs a TOP view (see angles.topDown).
insert.use: what the story needs us to notice: the result on the screen, the ring, the empty plate, the clock, the money, the knock on the door; also to cover time and to cut between two shots of the same person
insert.avoid: an insert of something that will not matter; readable text held shorter than its reading time (see rules.textReadTime)
insert.flat2d: Cheapest bridge shot in the book: one prop, one background colour, maybe one hand.

9:16.note: Centre it; keep it above y 0.6 (caption tray).

16:9.note: Thirds work; a hand entering from the side reads well.

sideBySide.use: walking together, sitting on a bench/rickshaw, watching something together, a united front

faceToFace.use: confrontation, negotiation, romance (the gap between them is the story)

deep.views: near: three or back-three; far: front or three
deep.use: 9:16 two-shots; one listening in the foreground while the other talks; power (the bigger one dominates)

twoShot.frameBottom: set by the size chosen for the nearer person
twoShot.widthNeed: frameWidth >= (distance between the two face centres + 2.0 heads) / 0.84

9:16.faceToFace0.8m: frame W 1.48 m (man) -> wider than a full shot (1.08 m): full/wide
9:16.rule: In 9:16 a side-by-side or face-to-face two-shot is always full/wide unless the two are stacked in depth (variant deep).

16:9.medium: works when face centres <= 0.75 m apart

twoShot.use: relationship at a glance; re-establish geography after singles; humour (reaction of both in one frame)
twoShot.avoid: both people in front view talking to the lens (they must angle 30-90 deg toward each other); heads at exactly the same height and size (flat, 'twinning')

9:16.note: Prefer deep. Near person head 0.18-0.28 of frame height at x 0.3-0.4; far person 0.1-0.16 at x 0.6-0.7.

16:9.note: sideBySide and faceToFace both fine at mediumWide; medium when close.

group.definition: 3 or more people whose faces are readable (head >= 0.04 of frame height) in one frame

9:16.beyond: stack in depth (triangle) or go wide and cut to singles for reactions

group.staging: triangle: nearest person largest; faces at 3 different heights and x positions; nobody's face overlapping another's
group.use: family scenes, a classroom, a committee, friends at a tea stall; re-establish who is where
group.avoid: lining everyone up on one horizontal row facing camera (school photo look) unless it is a deliberate tableau

9:16.note: Use height: people on two or three depth rows. Max 2 readable faces side by side.

16:9.note: Rows across are fine; still vary heights (someone sits, someone stands).

cameraHeight.twoPeople: use the eye height of the person whose side we are on; if neutral, the mean of both

horizon.behindHead: middle of the back wall / distant trees and houses at eye height

eyeLevel.subjectView: any; dialogue singles three (yaw 20-45 deg toward the partner); profile two-shots side

flat2dFake.how: native: the front-view pieces were drawn for about this height (h_ref 1.5 m). Nothing to fake.

eyeLevel.use: neutral, equal, honest; the default (60-75 % of shots in a calm film); people talking as equals
eyeLevel.avoid: 100 % of shots (the flat 'TV' look); a scene about power, fear or smallness

9:16.note: eyes on the horizon at 0.3-0.37 in CU/MCU

16:9.note: same rule; horizon 0.33-0.38

cameraHeight.rule: eye-0.5 to eye-0.9 m (about chest-to-hip height of the subject)

horizon.behindHead: upper wall, ceiling line, sky, treetops: backgroundHeightBehindEyes = h + (eye - h) * D/d

low.subjectView: front or three; when they look at the (lower) partner their eyes aim 10-20 deg below level

flat2dFake.horizon: lower it so it crosses the subject at chest/hip height; out of frame below in MS/CU
flat2dFake.personScaleNote: affine stretch of the whole character, anchored at the feet; if the rig allows head scale, head 0.96-0.98
flat2dFake.foreground: one near object along the bottom edge at 0.3-0.5 x subject depth (2-3x size): table edge, grass, a bicycle wheel, a raised hand
flat2dFake.showAbove: interiors need a ceiling strip (flat colour band with a ceiling fan or beams) whenever the frame reaches above 2.6 m
flat2dFake.hide: every horizontal surface whose drawn top lies between h and 1.5 m (desks, counters, a shop's taak at 0.75-1.0 m): crop it below the frame or cover it

low.needs: ceiling strip piece with a ceiling fan (cheap). Nothing else.
low.use: power, authority, threat (landlord, strict headmaster, a bully, a villain); heroism and triumph (the boy who just won the match); a parent seen by a small child; a tall tree, a minaret, a building towering
low.avoid: a person praying (never); a victim; ordinary talk; giving every character low angles (everyone becomes a hero, the angle stops meaning anything)

9:16.note: tall frame shows lots of ceiling/sky above the head: use it (fan, sky, branches)

16:9.note: keep a foreground element on the low corner to sell the height

metres.onChild: an adult's eye height (1.42-1.54) is already high on a child (eye 1.04)

horizon.behindHead: floor or ground fills the space behind the head; no sky

high.subjectView: front or three; when they look at the (higher) partner their eyes aim 10-25 deg above level

flat2dFake.horizon: raise it above the head (out of frame in MS/CU; near the top in wides)
flat2dFake.personScaleNote: affine squash anchored at the feet; head scale 1.02-1.04 if the rig allows
flat2dFake.floor: more floor shows: needs a floor texture/rug/pati pattern tile
flat2dFake.hide: tables and beds below h show 1.6-2.5x too little top (topBandRatio): crop them out, cover with foreground, or scale their top layer by the ratio

high.needs: floor texture tiles; optionally furniture with the top surface as its own layer
high.use: small, alone, defeated, watched; a child seen by an adult; someone sitting on the floor after bad news; a lost child in a crowd; the moment of being judged
high.avoid: making the powerful person look small by accident; looking down steeply on people praying (if ever, gentle: <= eye+0.5 m and from >= 3 m)

9:16.note: floor fills the tall frame: needs texture, or it looks empty

16:9.note: works well with negative space on one side for loneliness

cameraHeight.rule: 1.0-3.0 m above the top of the subject, pitch -90 deg

flat2dFake.objects: cheap for FLAT things: draw only the top view of that one object (plate of bhat and dal, a letter, a phone on a table, ludo board, exam paper with a hand writing, a map). Flat colour top views are simple shapes.

topDown.needs: top-view people (head and shoulders from above; poses: standing, sitting on a mat, lying on a bed, lying on a floor mat), top views of table, bed with mosquito net, jainamaz, pati/shital pati, plates and bowls, a boat
topDown.possibleWithFrontPieces: no for people; partly for flat objects
topDown.use: a family meal from above; writing an exam; a person lying awake at night; a pattern (students in rows, boats on a ghat); fate
topDown.avoid: close-ups of people praying from above; holding > 3 s with no context

9:16.note: tall frame: a person lying on a bed fits head-to-foot

16:9.note: good for tables seen across

cameraHeight.rule: near person's shoulder to eye height: A.eye-0.2 to A.eye

overShoulder.placement: 0.4-0.8 m behind A, 0.2-0.4 m to A's side on the established camera side of the 180 line

nearPerson.view: back or threeBack (yaw 135-165): back of the head, the cheek edge, one shoulder
nearPerson.whichShoulder: the shoulder on the camera side of the line: A facing screen-right -> A's right shoulder; facing screen-left -> left shoulder
nearPerson.headClearance: A's head stays >= 0.05 of frame width away from B's face

farPerson.eyes: look at A's eyes: 5-15 deg off the lens, on A's side

variants.dirtySingle: A shows as a sliver <= 0.1 of frame width
variants.cleanSingle: A out of frame, B framed as if A were there (same eyes direction)

overShoulder.reverse: mirror everything: B near on the right edge, A far at faceX 0.32-0.4 (16:9) / 0.35-0.45 (9:16); same size and eyeLine (rules.shotReverseShotMatch)

flat2dFake.near: A's back or threeBack head-and-shoulder at 2-3x B's scale, cropped by the frame edge, blurred and darkened
flat2dFake.far: B on the existing front set
flat2dFake.reverseBackground: the wall behind A in the reverse does not exist in a front-view set. Cheap first: blur it to soft colour blocks in the room palette; or reuse a door/window/almirah piece; or reframe A against a plain wall colour. Best: draw a 'reverse wall' for each main set.

overShoulder.needs: back/threeBack views (exist), a blur filter, reverse-wall backgrounds (new drawings, or the blur fake)
overShoulder.use: the standard way to cover a conversation; confrontation, interrogation, interviews, romance; makes the viewer stand with A
overShoulder.avoid: A's head covering B's face; mixing dirty and clean singles inside one exchange; crossing the line on the reverse

9:16.note: the main 9:16 dialogue tool (vertical microdramas cut OTS A / OTS B); A's shoulder in the lower corner, B's face high and central

16:9.note: A on one edge, B on the opposite third

cameraHeight.rule: the looker's eye height at the looker's position

horizon.crossesSubjectAt: the looker's eye height on every standing person

pov.subjectView: a person who looks at the looker: front, eyes INTO the lens (+-2 deg). Objects: as seen.

flat2dFake.breathing: handheld 0.2-0.4 % of the short side, 0.3-0.6 Hz for a person; none for a fixed view (window, CCTV)
flat2dFake.hands: optional POV hands in the lower 0.3 of the frame (holding a phone/letter/handlebar): needs first-person hand drawings
flat2dFake.blink: optional: 3-4 frame close to black for waking up or fainting

pov.needs: front views looking into the lens (exist); POV hands (new, optional)
pov.pattern: looker (CU, eyes off-screen) -> POV -> looker reacts (the Kuleshov sandwich)
pov.use: what someone sees: the letter, the result list on the notice board, the person at the door, the bus leaving; a child's view up at adults (camera 1.0 m); fear of someone approaching; love (a smile seen)
pov.avoid: a POV from someone praying; > 3 s before cutting back to the looker; eyes into the lens outside a POV or a direct address

9:16.note: centred subject, works naturally (phone = eyes)

16:9.note: fine; optional slight vignette

cameraHeight.rule: mean eye height of the two

profile.placement: camera perpendicular to the line between them (90 +- 10 deg)

9:16.rule: mediumWide only if they stand <= 0.6 m apart (faces x 0.3-0.38 and 0.62-0.7); else full/wide

flat2dFake.how: native to flat 2D: side views exist and the set stays front-on. The gap between them is the drama: 0.3 m intimate/fight, 0.8 m talk, 1.5 m distance.

profile.use: a confrontation between equals; negotiation; a romance stand-off; two kids comparing marbles; seated talk at a table or on a bench (both side on)
profile.avoid: whole conversations in profile (eyes hard to read: cut to three-quarter singles for key lines); both heads at the same height and size (twinning)

9:16.note: hard: they must be close; use as an accent

16:9.note: a classic

flat2dFake.how: roll the frame with the tilt parameter (free)
flat2dFake.coverage: the set must cover the rotated frame: 9:16 at 15 deg needs 1.43x the frame width and 1.11x its height (geometry.dutchCoverage)
flat2dFake.drift: optional roll change of 2-5 deg over the shot for fever, drunkenness, dizziness
flat2dFake.opposite: in a confrontation tilt A's singles +12 deg and B's -12 deg

dutch.use: unease, plotting, confusion after shocking news, fever or dizziness, a dream going wrong, the chaos of a scuffle (non-graphic), parody
dutch.avoid: faith moments (never); calm or happy scenes; more than 2-3 in a row unless the whole sequence is 'wrong'; random tilt directions

16:9.note: needs more set height

horizon.behindHead: sky or ceiling fills 60-80 % of the frame

worm.subjectView: front or three; footsteps: feet in front view

flat2dFake.cheap: horizon at the ankles, floorScale 0.05-0.27, a giant foreground (grass blades, pebbles, a shoe, a cricket ball) at 0.1-0.3 x subject depth (3-10x size), personScaleY 1.05-1.08
flat2dFake.true: looking steeply up (converging verticals, under the chin, nostrils, the fan from below) needs under-view drawings or a perspective mesh warp

worm.needs: giant foreground props (reuse props at big scale); for the true version: under-views or a mesh warp
worm.use: a giant/hero/villain entrance; a child's or a cat's view; shoes stepping in; a ball rolling at camera; a towering tree, minaret or building
worm.avoid: people praying; ordinary talk; more than once a minute

16:9.note: wide foreground across the bottom

horizon.crossesSubjectAt: none or at the very top

flat2dFake.true: needs a map kit of top views

bird.needs: map kit (top views): tin roofs, thatch roofs, concrete roofs, paddy fields (green/gold patches), river ribbon, boats from above, roads with rickshaws/CNG/buses from above, round tree canopies, ponds, people as head-and-shoulder dots, umbrellas
bird.use: opening and ending; a journey's progress (a boat on a wide river); a whole village or city; floods; a crowd or an Eid jamaat from far and high (respectful); a chase map
bird.avoid: holding > 4 s without a move; expecting faces to read

16:9.note: classic drone vista

cameraHeight.rule: 3-6 m (a rooftop, a balcony, a tree)

horizon.frac: -0.1 to 0.15 (at or above the top edge)

flat2dFake.how: front-view pieces in 3-6 depth rows, each row scaled by depth and raised toward the horizon; floorScale 2-4x so the ground band needs a texture (fields, road, courtyard). Reads like a miniature painting or a picture book.
flat2dFake.accept: roofs show only as drawn in front view: fine in this style

elevatedWide.needs: ground textures; enough set pieces to fill rows
elevatedWide.use: the cheap stand-in for bird: a village lane, a market, a school yard, a ghat
elevatedWide.avoid: pretending it is a drone shot (do not push it past 6 m)

9:16.note: 5-6 rows fill the tall frame

16:9.note: 3-4 rows

flat2dFake.how: native (it is just a lower camera): adults' heads end up 0.4-0.6 m above the horizon, tables show their undersides edge-on, so crop tabletops above 1.0 m

childHeight.use: any story told from a child's side: the classroom, the market, a parent's anger, a festival
childHeight.avoid: switching between child height and adult height inside one exchange without a reason

9:16.note: adults get cut at the chest in MS: let them lean down into the frame

16:9.note: same

cameraHeight.rule: eye level of the main subject

frontalTableau.subjectView: front (looking slightly off lens, 5-10 deg) or side for people walking across

flat2dFake.how: native: the camera is square to the back wall, the room is symmetrical, people stand in one plane. This is where flat 2D looks most intentional.

frontalTableau.use: comedy deadpan, formal moments (school assembly, a courtroom, a wedding stage), introductions of a family, faith settings at a respectful distance, title shots
frontalTableau.avoid: dialogue coverage (use singles and OTS); making every shot symmetrical

9:16.note: subject at x 0.5 +- 0.02

16:9.note: subject at x 0.5 or symmetrical pairs

cameraHeight.rule: eye level or slightly high, 1.5-3 m behind the subject

flat2dFake.how: the subject's back view in the foreground (0.3-0.5 of the frame height), the thing they look at beyond it (river, road, closed door, a grave, a train leaving)

backView.use: longing, leaving, contemplation, watching someone go, standing at a grave, looking at the sea; prayer seen respectfully from behind
backView.avoid: using it to hide a face during the key emotion (follow with a front CU)

9:16.note: subject low-centre, the view above

16:9.note: subject on a third, the view across

flat2dFake.how: a door, window, bars, mosquito net, rickshaw hood, bamboo fence or shop shutter in the foreground at 0.3-0.6 x subject depth, darkened 20-40 %; the subject inside the opening

throughFrame.use: watched, trapped, outsider looking in, eavesdropping, longing, a secret
throughFrame.avoid: covering the face in the key moment

9:16.note: a vertical door opening fits 9:16 perfectly

16:9.note: a window works best

static.use: the default (about 70-85 % of shots in calm talk); comedy timing; faith moments; anything where acting carries the beat
static.avoid: a static wide held > 4 s while nothing moves in it (use parallaxDrift or cut)

creep.anchor: the subject's eyes keep their frame position
creep.use: a long line or a long silence that should grow heavier; waiting; a confession; keeps a long 9:16 hold alive

pushIn.anchor: scale about the eyes so the face does not drift into the caption tray

modes.zoom: scale frameW only: works today, no parallax (reads as a zoom lens)
modes.dolly: move camera z forward by 20-45 % of the subject distance: background shrinks less than the subject grows, foreground grows faster. Reads as real cinema; prefer when the engine can.

pushIn.use: a realisation, a decision forming, a memory arriving, rising tension in a line, the turn of a scene
pushIn.avoid: calm talk (moves are rare there); two push-ins in a row; pushing in while the subject walks away; with any other move at once

pullOut.speedLimit: peak <= 30 % frame-width change per second; slower than the push it mirrors
pullOut.use: isolation (a person alone in a big empty room/field); revealing the context (the 'he is in hospital' reveal); the ending of a film; leaving a scene
pullOut.avoid: revealing a set that is not drawn wide enough (check the set covers the final frame)

panLeft.speedLimit: geometry.panSpeedLimit (9:16 width crossed in >= 3.2 s, 16:9 in >= 5.6 s without motion blur)
panLeft.flat2d: A real pan rotates the camera, so NOTHING shows parallax: slide all layers together. Correct and cheap.
panLeft.use: follow a moving subject; reveal what someone is looking at; connect two people in one space (the 'pan to the listener')
panLeft.avoid: panning across a set that is not wide enough; slow pans in fast films (cut instead); pans back and forth between speakers (soap-opera look) unless it is a comic choice

panRight.use: as panLeft; left-to-right reads as moving forward/away from home in left-to-right reading cultures (Bangla reads left to right)

tiltUp.speedLimit: 9:16: frame height crossed in >= 5.6 s without blur; 16:9: >= 3.2 s
tiltUp.flat2d: A level shift-camera 'tilt' slides layers together (no parallax), like a pan. True pitch (converging verticals) is not available.
tiltUp.use: hero reveal from shoes to face (2-4 s); a tree, minaret or tower bottom to top; from a face up to the sky (hope, prayer ending, death handled gently)
tiltUp.avoid: tilting up on a person praying to make them look grand; revealing an undrawn ceiling

tiltDown.use: from the sky down to the village (opening); from a face down to the thing in their hands (the letter, the result); from a sign down to the shop

trackSide.parallax: automatic from depth: layer speed = cameraSpeed * subjectDepth / layerDepth. Add 1-2 foreground posts/trees/rickshaws at 0.3-0.5 x subject depth: they pass at 2-3x and sell the speed; give them motion blur.
trackSide.use: walking and talking; a rickshaw or bus ride; a chase; a child running to school
trackSide.avoid: tracking a person who stands still; a set that ends before the move does

followBehind.flat2d: the walker (back view walk cycle) keeps a constant size; every set layer scales up as the camera approaches (camera z). Without camera z: use a static camera and let the walker walk away (shrinking) instead.
followBehind.needs: back-view walk cycle; camera z (or per-layer scale animation)
followBehind.use: entering a new world (first day at school, arriving in Dhaka); suspense (walking into a dark room); following someone through a crowd
followBehind.avoid: long follows with no destination reveal

lead.flat2d: front-view walk toward the camera while the camera retreats at the same speed: the walker stays the same size, set layers shrink. Needs camera z.
lead.use: walk-and-talk with faces visible; a determined walk; two friends on a village path
lead.avoid: very long leads (> 8 s) in short films

crane.flat2d: Animate camera height. With a level shift camera the horizon stays at the same frame row; every ground layer slides DOWN by k*dh/d (near layers faster): vertical parallax. The floor band grows with h; front-view tabletops get wrong past about h 2.2 m (crop them out). Add a small tilt down to keep the subject in frame.
crane.use: ending a film (rise and leave the characters); revealing a crowd or a flooded village; a moment of release after tension
crane.avoid: rising inside a room with no ceiling drawn; more than one per film

variants.craneDown: 6 m -> 1.5 m over 3-6 s: descend from the sky into the street to open a film

handheld.type: texture (may sit under one real move)
handheld.noise: smooth (simplex/Perlin) noise, 2 octaves; never per-frame random values
handheld.overscan: scale the frame up 2-4 % so shake never shows the set edge
handheld.use: documentary feel, tension, chases, POV, a crowd, panic
handheld.avoid: prayer and faith moments; calm dialogue; inserts with text; under a zoomPunch

whipPan.cutInside: put the cut on the most blurred frame; the incoming shot whips in the SAME direction
whipPan.use: energy; jumping to another place or time ('meanwhile'); comedy; a sudden look
whipPan.avoid: calm and faith scenes; more than 2 per minute

focusPull.timing: start 4-8 frames after the new subject starts to move or speak
focusPull.flat2d: Blur whole depth layers (geometry.blur). Flat colour blurs beautifully; cheap in canvas/CSS filters.
focusPull.use: shift attention from near to far (someone appears in the doorway behind); OTS emphasis; a tear in focus then the photo behind
focusPull.avoid: pulling to an empty plane; pulling in every shot

zoomPunch.after: hold to the end of the shot, or snap back in 4-6 frames after 0.5-1.0 s
zoomPunch.anchor: the eyes keep their frame position
zoomPunch.timing: land on the stressed syllable of the key word, or 2-4 frames after a reaction starts

variants.doublePunch: x0.9 then x0.82 on two beats 8-15 frames apart: comic overkill / soap-opera parody

zoomPunch.use: comedy emphasis, a punchline, an explainer's key word, a sudden 'what?!' reaction
zoomPunch.avoid: serious grief, faith, and any scene that should feel real; stacking with handheld

impactShake.trigger: starts on the impact frame, exponential decay
impactShake.use: thunder, a door slam, a fall, a bus braking hard, a cricket ball hitting the stumps, a heavy sack dropped
impactShake.avoid: violence shown for its own sake; more than 1 per 10 s

parallaxDrift.type: texture-level move (counts as the one move)
parallaxDrift.flat2d: The cheapest 'cinematic' move in flat 2D: a tiny sideways truck; depth layers slide at different speeds and the picture gains depth.
parallaxDrift.use: establishing wides, landscapes, long calm singles, title cards over a set
parallaxDrift.avoid: dialogue cutting (cutting between drifting shots that drift in opposite directions is jarring)

dollyZoom.flat2d: possible with depth layers: keep the subject's size, scale background layers by their depth ratio as camera z changes
dollyZoom.use: a shocking realisation (the exam result, a betrayal); at most once per film

arc.fake: +-10-15 deg: slide background layers opposite to the subject (parallax) and swap the person's view front->three at the midpoint, hidden by a foreground wipe
arc.needs: every set piece and person in several views
arc.use: a reunion, a dizzy romance, a hero moment
arc.avoid: until the library has multi-view sets

amount.cameraH_m: 6 -> 1.5 (sky into the street), 2.5 -> 1.5 (over a wall into a yard)

craneDown.flat2d: the reverse of crane: ground layers slide UP by k*dh/d as the camera comes down; the floor band shrinks
craneDown.use: opening a film: from the sky or a rooftop down into the lane where the story starts
craneDown.avoid: more than one per film; descending into a room with no ceiling drawn

moveRules.calmTalkShare: in calm dialogue <= 1 moving shot (not counting creep/parallaxDrift) per 5 shots
moveRules.settle: a move into a cut: either finish the move and hold >= 0.4 s (12 f), or cut mid-move into a shot moving the same direction at a similar speed

hardCut.rule: Picture and sound change on the same frame.
hardCut.avoid: between two shots of the same size and angle on the same person (rules.jumpCut)

cutOnAction.rule: Start a movement in shot A and finish it in shot B (sit down, stand up, turn, open a door, lift a cup, throw).

timing.cutPoint: 1/3 to 1/2 into the action, during the fastest part, not after it lands

cutOnAction.why: Viewers prefer a straight match (0 frames) on average; a few frames either way barely matter. Motion AFTER the cut is what hides it, so the incoming shot must keep moving for >= 10 frames.
cutOnAction.sizeChange: >= 1 ladder step (wide -> medium, medium -> closeUp) or a view change
cutOnAction.use: joining a wide and a close shot of one action; hiding a size change; energy
cutOnAction.avoid: cutting after the action has stopped (the cut shows)

matchCut.rule: Join two different things that share a shape, position, colour or movement (a round roti -> the full moon; a spinning wheel -> a spinning fan; a falling kite -> a falling leaf).
matchCut.use: jumping in time or place with elegance; openings; montage transitions; memory
matchCut.avoid: forcing it (if the shapes differ by more than the tolerance, use a dissolve)

eyelineMatch.rule: A looks off-screen; cut to what A looks at, seen from about A's position and height; then (often) back to A.
eyelineMatch.geometry: A's gaze direction (left/right, up/down) predicts where the target is; the target shot's camera height = A's eye height (or the POV).
eyelineMatch.use: showing what someone sees or wants; reveals; Kuleshov-style reactions
eyelineMatch.avoid: a look with no payoff; a target framed from an impossible height

reactionCut.rule: Cut to the listener when the line lands, not when it ends.
reactionCut.use: dialogue rhythm; comedy (the reaction IS the joke); bad news (the face receiving it matters more than the face giving it)
reactionCut.avoid: a reaction with no change in the face

jCut.rule: The sound of the NEXT shot starts before its picture.
jCut.use: a voice calls before we see the speaker; the azan or a train is heard before the new scene; smoothing dialogue so it feels like a real conversation
jCut.avoid: leading with a sound that belongs to nothing on screen later

lCut.rule: The sound of the PREVIOUS shot keeps playing over the next picture.
lCut.use: the speaker keeps talking while we watch the listener's reaction; a song or a mother's voice carries into the next scene
lCut.avoid: trailing a speaker's line under a shot where the speaker's mouth is visible and closed

fade.rule: From/to a flat colour (black by default; white for heaven/memory/purity).
fade.use: the start and end of a film; the end of a chapter; sleep; death handled gently
fade.avoid: inside a scene; in 15-30 s phone videos except at the very end (it costs precious seconds)

dissolve.rule: Shot A fades out while shot B fades in, overlapping.
dissolve.use: time passing; a memory starting or ending; softness (a lullaby, a sunset); joining two similar compositions (same room, later)
dissolve.avoid: between two shots in the same time (it says 'time passed'); under 8 frames (looks like a mistake)

cutToBlack.rule: Instant black; usually sound stops too (or one sound continues).
cutToBlack.use: shock; an unfinished sentence; the last frame of a film; a chapter hit
cutToBlack.avoid: more than once per short film

smashCut.rule: Abrupt jump from one intensity to its opposite (quiet -> loud, calm -> chaos, a promise -> its contradiction). Picture and sound change on the same frame; the incoming shot starts at its peak.
smashCut.pattern: 'I will never eat that.' -> SMASH -> him eating it.
smashCut.use: comedy; waking from a dream; a scream into silence

timeJump.rule: Show time passing with one of these, cheapest first.

sameFrameDissolve.how: same set and framing, people/props/light change, dissolve 30-60 f each; 2-4 steps

lightChange.how: 3 shots of the same place: day -> dusk -> night, 0.8-1.2 s each, hard cuts or 12 f dissolves

insert.how: clock, calendar, phone date, the moon, a candle burned down, rice grown in the field: 1.0-1.5 s

montage.how: 4-8 shots 0.6-1.2 s each on music beats

matchAcrossTime.how: matchCut on the same action years apart (a child's hand -> an adult's hand)

timeJump.use: any ellipsis of hours to years

crossCut.rule: Alternate between two places/people happening at the same time.
crossCut.use: phone calls; a race against time (the bus is leaving / she is running); a rescue
crossCut.avoid: switching without a clear question linking the two

cutaway.rule: Cut to something else in the same place (a clock, a cat, the window, the street), then back.
cutaway.use: breathing room; hiding a jump in time or a jump cut; showing the world
cutaway.avoid: cutaways that pull attention from the emotional line

montage.rule: A run of short shots that compresses a process or a period.

timing.onBeat: cut on music beats (every 2 beats at 90-120 bpm = 1.0-1.3 s)

montage.use: studying for exams, preparing for Eid, building a boat, a season changing, training for a match
montage.avoid: montages longer than 15 % of a short film

whiteFlash.rule: 2-4 frames of white (or the brightest palette colour) between two shots.
whiteFlash.use: a memory flashing back; a camera flash; lightning; a sudden idea
whiteFlash.avoid: repeated flashes (photosensitivity: never more than 3 flashes in any 1 s)

wipe.rule: A shape or edge pushes the old shot off the screen.
wipe.use: children's content, retro comedy, chapter breaks in explainers

irisOut.rule: A circle closes on the subject to black (classic cartoon).

jumpCutStyle.rule: Deliberate jump cuts inside one take of a person talking to camera, to remove pauses.

timing.punchInOnAlternateCuts: frameW x0.85-0.9 on every 2nd cut hides the jump

jumpCutStyle.use: direct-address explainers and narrator pieces only

objectWipe.rule: A foreground thing (a person, a rickshaw, a pillar, a passing bus) fills the frame for 3-6 frames; cut while it covers the frame.
objectWipe.use: hiding a cut in a 'one-shot' feel; changing place in a market or a street
objectWipe.avoid: using it twice in a row

soundBridge.rule: A sound connects two shots: a kettle whistle becomes a train whistle; a heartbeat becomes a drum.
soundBridge.avoid: when the two sounds are not alike

rulesInput.note: What the checker needs per shot. All tests below use only these fields plus the engine's project(point) -> frame (x, y).

moves: move keys active in the shot
shot.cutIn: cut key that joins this shot to the previous one

derived.gazeDirX(p): sign of the screen-x component of the gaze vector (yaw + eye offset)

rules.rule: In a scene where people interact, keep the camera on one side of the line through the two main people, so A stays left of B and each keeps their facing direction.
rules.test: Take the scene's first shot with both A and B visible (the master): s0 = sign(faceX(B) - faceX(A)). In every later shot with both visible, sign(faceX(B) - faceX(A)) must equal s0. In singles where A looks at B, screenDir(A) must equal s0 and screenDir(B) must equal -s0. In ground-plane terms: sign(cross(B - A, Camera - A)) is constant.
allowedCrossings: a shot taken ON the line (subject front-on |yaw| <= 15, or a POV)
a move that crosses the line inside the shot
a character crossing the frame and re-establishing
a cutaway/insert followed by a new master
rules.fix: mirror the offending shot (cheap; then run mirrorSafety), or re-stage, or add one of the allowed bridges

rules.rule: A movement that continues across cuts (a walk, a chase, a journey) keeps the same screen direction.
rules.test: For consecutive shots sharing a movementId: sign(screen vx of the mover) is the same. Ignore shots where |vx| < 0.02 frame widths/s (moving toward/away from camera = neutral).

convention.outward: +1 (left to right): home -> school, village -> Dhaka, leaving
convention.note: Bangla reads left to right, so the Western convention holds; keep it consistent within a film.

rules.fix: mirror the shot; or insert a neutral shot (head-on or tail-away); or show the turn on screen

rules.rule: Two people looking at each other in separate shots look in opposite screen directions (A looks right -> B looks left).
rules.test: Consecutive singles X (A, eyeTarget B, B not visible) and Y (B, eyeTarget A, A not visible): gazeDirX(A) = -gazeDirX(B), both non-zero, and the gaze is 5-35 deg off the lens. If A is left in the master, gazeDirX(A) = +1.
rules.fix: set yaw/eye direction from the master positions (rig parameters, free) or mirror one shot

rules.rule: Vertical gaze matches real heights: the taller or standing person looks down, the shorter or seated one looks up.
rules.test: d = eyeH(A) - eyeH(B) (world). If d > 0.15 m: gazePitch(A) = -atan(d / dist) +- 10 deg and gazePitch(B) = +atan(d / dist) +- 10 deg. If |d| <= 0.15 m both |gazePitch| <= 8 deg.
rules.fix: compute pitch = atan2(d, horizontal distance) and set the eye targets

rules.rule: The gap above the head matches the shot size.
rules.test: headTopY must lie within sizes[size].frameTop.headroom (format value). Negative (cropped) only for closeUp (>= allowCrop -0.12) and extremeClose. Fail 'sinking' if headroom > max + 0.05.
rules.fix: lookAt.y += (actualHeadTopY - targetHeadTopY) * frameH

rules.rule: Leave more space in front of a face (where it looks) or a mover (where it goes) than behind.
rules.test: For a person with |yaw| >= 20 or |vx| > 0: ahead = 1 - faceX if screenDir = +1, else faceX; behind = 1 - ahead. Looks: ahead/behind >= 1.12 (9:16), >= 1.5 (16:9). Movers: >= 1.3 (9:16), >= 1.8 (16:9). 9:16 closeUp and extremeClose are exempt (the face fills the width; show direction with yaw and eyes).
exceptions: tag shortSide: deliberate trapped/threat framing, max 3 s
rules.fix: shift lookAt.x so faceX hits sizes[size].subjectPos

rules.rule: Never cut between two shots of the same subject at the same size and angle.
rules.test: Consecutive shots with the same main subject: r = max(frameH_heads1, frameH_heads2) / min(...). Angle change = |yaw1 - yaw2| (view change) and vertical change = atan(|h1 - h2| / subjectDistance). FAIL if r < 1.25 and yaw change < 30 deg and vertical change < 15 deg. WARN if 1.25 <= r < 1.4 with no other change.
rules.fix: change size by >= 1 ladder step (2 is better), or change the view (front -> three = 45 deg), or put a reaction/insert between them

rules.rule: Every cut on the same subject changes size by at least one ladder step (frame-height ratio >= 1.4) or angle by at least 30 deg (the 30-degree rule).
rules.test: For same-subject cuts: r >= 1.4 OR yaw change >= 30 OR vertical angle change >= 15 deg (about 0.5 m of camera height at 2 m) OR a change of angle family (eyeLevel -> overShoulder, profile, high, low).
rules.flat2dNote: The flat engine cannot orbit; 'angle' changes come from the person's view (front/three/side), camera height, OTS vs clean, and mirroring for reverses.
rules.fix: as jumpCut

rules.rule: In human singles the eyes sit near the upper third.
rules.test: medium to closeUp: eyeY in [0.22, 0.4]; mediumWide/full: eyeY <= 0.25; extremeClose variants and inserts exempt. FAIL if eyeY > 0.5 in any single from medium inward.
rules.fix: lookAt.y correction as headroom

rules.rule: Frame edges never cut a person at a joint (neck, shoulders line, elbows, waist line, wrists, knees, ankles).
rules.test: For each visible person, convert where the top/bottom edge crosses them into head units from headTop; fail if it falls inside any landmarks.joints band. For side edges: warn if a wrist or elbow lies within 0.03 of frame width of the edge.
rules.fix: move the edge to the nearest landmarks.safeCuts value (prefer the one that keeps the planned size)

rules.rule: A shot lasts long enough to be read on a phone.
rules.test: duration >= sizes[size].minHold * clutter * audience. clutter = clamp(1 + 0.15 * (significantElements - 3), 1, 1.6). audience: kids profile x1.5. Plus text: see textReadTime. Absolute floor 0.4 s (12 f); montage/flash shots 0.2 s (6 f). The first shot of a film >= 1.5 s.
rules.fix: extend the shot, simplify the frame, or merge it with the next

rules.rule: No dead air: a shot ends once it has said its thing.
rules.test: WARN if a static shot has no character action (mouth or limb animation < 15 % of its time) for > 4 s (9:16) / > 5 s (16:9); WARN on any shot > 8 s in films <= 60 s unless tagged hold.
rules.fix: cut, add a creep/parallaxDrift, or give the character an action

rules.rule: 3+ readable faces make a group shot; a phone frame holds only 2 readable expressions side by side.
rules.test: n = faces with headFrac >= 0.04. n >= 3 -> class group. 9:16: FAIL if n >= 3 standing side by side (all within 0.5 m depth) and the beat needs expressions (headFrac >= 0.10). 16:9: max 7 readable expressions across.
rules.fix: stack in depth (triangle), or go wide and cut to singles for reactions

rules.rule: Whenever a mouth is readable on screen, it moves only if that person is speaking.
rules.test: For each frame of a line by S, for each visible P with view in {front, three, side} and headFrac >= 0.06: P = S -> mouth = speaking; P != S -> mouth in {closed, idle}. S with headFrac < 0.06 -> simple flap allowed; S in back/threeBack view or off screen -> fine (voice off).
rules.fix: animate visemes for S; close the listener's mouth

rules.rule: The audience sees who is talking.
rules.test: Each line: speaker visible (face readable) >= 50 % of its duration unless the line's picture is a deliberate reaction/J/L cut. A new speaker's first line: speaker visible within 1.0 s of the line start. keyLine-tagged lines: speaker visible >= 70 % or the listener's reaction is the planned payoff.
rules.fix: move the cut or add a shot of the speaker

rules.rule: The horizon crosses every standing person at the same real height: the camera height.
rules.test: For each standing person on the same floor: hp = stature * (feetY - horizonY) / (feetY - headTopY). |hp - camera.h| <= max(0.05 m, 0.03 * stature), and any two people differ by <= 0.08 m.
rules.fix: that person's depth scale or feet position is wrong (floating or mis-sized): recompute from depth

rules.rule: Horizontal surfaces show their tops only below camera height, and front-view pieces only near the height they were drawn for.
rules.test: For each visible piece with a top at height s (world sizes, Brief 5): if s > h + 0.08 and the piece shows a drawn top -> FAIL. topBandRatio = (h - s) / (1.5 - s); WARN if the top is visible and the ratio is outside [0.7, 1.4].
rules.fix: crop the surface out, cover it with foreground, use a no-top variant, or scale the piece's top layer by the ratio

rules.rule: In 9:16, faces of key characters, on-screen text and the key prop stay out of the platform UI.
rules.test: For >= 90 % of the shot, those boxes are inside formats['9:16'].safeZones.keySafe (x 0.06-0.82, y 0.15-0.65). Background faces exempt.
rules.fix: shift lookAt or change size

rules.rule: A feeling that matters is shown big enough to read.
rules.test: Shots holding an emotionBeat: main face headFrac >= 0.27 (9:16), >= 0.38 for keyLine beats; 16:9 >= 0.38 for key beats (phones letterbox 16:9).
rules.fix: go one or two sizes tighter or pushIn

rules.rule: No more than 3 close-ups in a row, and no close-up of someone who is not feeling anything.
rules.test: Consecutive shots with size in {closeUp, extremeClose} <= 3. In any 10 shots CU+ECU <= 50 % (9:16), <= 35 % (16:9). WARN on a CU whose subject has no emotion change and no line.
rules.fix: insert a mediumClose, an OTS, a two-shot or an insert

rules.rule: Never two camera moves at once (textures like handheld may sit under one move).
rules.test: Active moves in a shot minus moveRules.textureAllowedUnderOneMove: count <= 1, unless the pair is in moveRules.allowedPairs.
rules.fix: split into two shots or drop one move

rules.rule: Don't cut a move off mid-way into a still shot.
rules.test: If camera speed in the last 6 frames > 10 % of the move's peak, the next shot must start with a move in the same direction at 0.5-1.5x the speed; otherwise the move must end >= 12 frames before the cut.
rules.fix: end the move earlier, or start the next shot moving

rules.rule: When the place changes, show it.
rules.test: When locationId changes, one of the first 3 shots (or the first 6 s) has size in {extremeWide, wide, full} or angle in {bird, elevatedWide}. Tag delayedEstablish: it must come before the scene's midpoint.
rules.fix: add an establishing wide (a 1.5-2.5 s parallaxDrift is enough)

rules.rule: Paired singles in a conversation mirror each other.
rules.test: For alternating singles of A and B: same size key, |eyeY_A - eyeY_B| <= 0.03, faceX_B = 1 - faceX_A +- 0.05, camera height relative to each one's eyes within 0.1 m, same angle family (both OTS or both clean).
exceptions: tag powerShift: one side deliberately lower/closer
rules.fix: copy A's framing values to B mirrored

rules.rule: In fast cutting, the next point of interest appears near where the eye already is.
rules.test: For cuts where both shots are < 1.5 s: distance between the focal point (main face centre or key prop) on the last outgoing frame and the first incoming frame <= 0.3 of the frame diagonal.
rules.fix: re-frame the incoming shot so its face lands near the previous one (9:16 centre framing makes this easy)

rules.rule: The camera never shows past the edge of a drawn set.
rules.test: For every frame (moves, handheld overscan and dutch roll included), the rotated frame rectangle is inside the drawn area of the layers behind the subject. Dutch: see geometry.dutchCoverage.
rules.fix: shrink frameW, limit the move, or extend the set

rules.rule: No strong horizontal line of the set touches a chin or the top of a head.
rules.test: Horizontal set lines (horizon, wall-floor line, table edge, window sill, shelf, roof line) with screen y within +- 0.08 head of a visible chinY or headTopY -> WARN. A non-horizon graphic line through the eyes -> WARN.
rules.fix: change camera height by >= 0.15 head equivalent, move lookAt.y, or move the person in depth

rules.rule: Standing people stand on the floor at the right size for their depth, with a contact shadow.
rules.test: feetY = project(feet at depth) within 0.005 of frame height; a contact-shadow layer exists under each visible foot.
rules.fix: snap feet to the ground plane; add the shadow (sizes.full.flat2d)

rules.rule: Characters look into the lens only in a POV, a direct address, or a deliberate fourth-wall break.
rules.test: eyeTarget == 'lens' requires a tag in {pov, directAddress}; otherwise the gaze is >= 5 deg off the lens.
rules.fix: aim the eyes at the partner's position

rules.rule: A mirrored (flipped) shot must not contain anything with a correct side.
rules.test: If camera.mirrored: FAIL if the frame contains readable text (Bangla or English signs, books, phone screens, number plates), a clock or watch face, a person eating, giving or receiving with the right hand, a vehicle whose driving side shows (Bangladesh drives on the LEFT: steering on the right), asymmetric character marks (side parting, mole, scar, watch arm), a known landmark, a cricketer's batting side, or anyone praying.
rules.fix: re-stage instead of mirroring, or swap that element for its own correctly-sided version

rules.rule: Prayer and faith moments are shot calmly and respectfully, for every faith.
rules.test: Shots tagged faith: angle not in {low, worm, dutch}; moves not in {zoomPunch, whipPan, impactShake, dollyZoom} and handheld at most 'calm'; cutIn/cutOut not in {smashCut, wipe, irisOut}. Posture sajdah: size not in {closeUp, extremeClose, mediumClose}. No POV from a praying person. No camera directly in front of a praying person closer than 2 m (do not stand between them and the qibla). High angles: h <= eye + 0.5 m and distance >= 3 m.
contentRules: never depict any prophet; show a place, light or calligraphy instead
holy books never on the floor or under feet in frame
no comic sound hits on a prayer
rules.fix: use profile, backView or a respectful wide at eye level

rules.rule: Everyone praying together faces the same way, and that way stays consistent across cuts.
rules.test: Within a prayer scene, all people with posture in {stand, ruku, sajdah, sit} and tag faith share one facing direction (world); across shots the screen direction of that facing follows line180 logic. Mirroring is forbidden.
rules.fix: fix yaw; re-stage the camera on one side of the prayer row

rules.rule: On-screen text stays up long enough to read.
rules.test: hold >= 0.5 s + characters / cps, with cps = 13 (adult Bangla), 17 (adult English), 9 (children). Minimum 0.83 s, maximum 7 s per caption.
rules.fix: lengthen the shot or shorten the text

rules.rule: Straight cuts in dialogue fall between words.
rules.test: A hardCut whose picture and sound change together must fall in a silence >= 4 frames, or <= 6 frames before the next line starts; never inside a word (word timings). With a J/L cut the picture may change anywhere, best within 6 frames of a sentence end or on a reaction.
rules.fix: slide the cut to the nearest gap, or make it a J/L cut

rules.rule: No more than 3 flashes in any 1 second.
rules.test: Count frame-to-frame luminance jumps of >= 10 % of full range across >= 25 % of the frame (lightning, whiteFlash, strobing): <= 3 per any 1 s window; avoid large saturated-red flashes.
rules.fix: space the flashes or soften them

rules.rule: Vary the camera.
rules.test: <= 4 consecutive shots at the same size; <= 6 consecutive at the same camera height (+- 0.2 m); in any 60 s: >= 4 size classes and >= 2 angle families, unless tagged tableauFilm.
rules.fix: swap in an insert, an OTS, a wide or a height change

rules.rule: Shot lengths breathe; they are not a metronome.
rules.test: In scenes of >= 6 shots, the coefficient of variation of shot lengths >= 0.25 (montages cut on the beat are exempt).
rules.fix: lengthen the emotional holds, shorten the plain information shots

pace.note: ASL = average shot length. Ranges are for narrative 2D phone films; check the film against them after planning.

explainer.note: a visual change about every 3 s; a field sample of high-performing talking-head TikToks averaged 0.37 cuts/s, and medium pace (~0.33 cuts/s) kept viewers watching best in a test

kidsUnder7.note: very fast cartoons (scene change every 11 s) impaired 4-year-olds' executive function right after viewing vs a slow one (every 34 s); go slow for small children

references.hollywood: ASL fell from about 12 s (1930s) to about 2.5-4 s (2000s-2010s); fast action films 1.7-3 s
references.animatedFeatures: animated movies have shorter shots and more motion than live action
references.shortForm: creator advice says 'cut every 1-3 s'; treat this as marketing lore, not measured fact. Measured: ~2.7 s between cuts in strong talking-head TikToks
references.readingFaces: closer shots are read faster: close-ups can be shorter than wides (larger face + less clutter = faster)

bangladeshiTvDrama.production: most natoks are made in a few days on small budgets (many at 1-2 lakh taka; often about 70 % goes to the two lead actors) and released mainly on YouTube; Eid is the peak season
camera: dialogue covered with 1-2 cameras: MCU/CU singles and OTS, long dialogue scenes
frequent zoom-lens moves and slow push-ins on reactions; drone 'top shots' of rivers, roads and fields as establishing and transition shots
romance and longing carried by music montages, slow motion and glance exchanges rather than touch
3-camera set-ups for action or crowd moments
the Farooki/'Chabial' wave brought handheld naturalism, overlapping everyday dialogue, jump cuts and deadpan pans
frontal staging: actors often cheat toward the camera; the 180 line is kept loosely in fast productions
bangladeshiTvDrama.status: observed conventions from viewing and press coverage, not a measured study

modernAnimatedShorts: design-led frames: bold silhouettes, centred 9:16 compositions, graphic match cuts
limited animation: held poses kept alive by camera (parallax drifts, punch-ins) and sound
vertical microdrama grammar: one subject per frame, alternating singles and OTS, close-ups dominate; conventional side-by-side two-shots are rare
on-screen text and captions as part of the picture
hollywoodContinuity: establish -> medium -> close; strict 180 line; eyeline matches; cut on action; the 30-degree rule
coverage from many angles, picked in the edit
camera moves motivated by character movement
whereTheyDiffer: Bangladeshi dramas hold dialogue shots longer and let music carry emotion; Hollywood cuts faster and uses silence and reaction shots
natoks stage more frontally (to the lens); Hollywood stages in depth and across the axis
natoks lean on zoom and drone; Hollywood leans on dolly/track and lens choice
faith and family scenes in Bangladesh are shot at a respectful distance and eye level; Hollywood may go close and dramatic
phone shorts (all traditions) are tighter, more centred and faster than any TV tradition
traditions.zancutBlend: Use Hollywood continuity (180, eyelines, cut on action) as the skeleton, Bangladeshi warmth and respect in what we show and how long we hold it, and phone-short tightness in framing.

setups.what: OTS pair (A over B, B over A)

minimumSet1min.plus: end on a wide (reuse setup 1 with a pullOut)
minimumSet1min.moves: <= 3 per minute: one parallaxDrift, one pushIn, one pullOut
minimumSet1min.cuts: hard cuts, 1-2 J-cuts, one reaction cut on the key line, one dissolve or fade
minimumSet1min.why: 6 setups + 1 accent give 4 size classes, 3 angle families and real shot/reverse-shot: enough to pass monotony and feel cinematic.

cheapMistakes.mistake: Everything in one front-on medium: people side by side at one depth, facing the lens, the horizon through every head.
cheapMistakes.fix: stage in depth, use OTS and singles, vary sizes (rules.monotony)

cheapMistakes.mistake: Characters talk to the lens or both look the same way; eyelines never meet.
cheapMistakes.fix: rules.eyelineMatch, three views turned 20-45 deg toward the partner

cheapMistakes.mistake: Feet off the ground plane, no contact shadow, sizes that ignore depth, heads that don't sit on one horizon.
Constant slow zooms on everything, linear (un-eased) keyframes, two moves at once, zooms with no parallax.
cheapMistakes.fix: moves only on turns of the story; eased; one at a time; parallax via depth layers

cheapMistakes.mistake: Shots held after they are read, lip-flap in static wides, metronome cutting, cutting only to whoever speaks (no reactions).

alsoCheap: mirrored shots with backwards Bangla text (rules.mirrorSafety)
the camera showing the edge of the set (rules.setCoverage)
